subject: DPA: Deployment-mode data governance and e-sign flow (Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Emily Jones <emily.jones@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA: Deployment-mode data governance and e-sign flow (Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Emily,

Thanks again for taking the time on Friday. Per our discussion at procurement, I wanted to surface a couple of items in the DPA draft that typically vary by deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC). I attached our annotated DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3_redlines.pdf) and a short dataflow spreadsheet that maps which controls apply where.

Key asks from Acme that I noted in the call:
- Clarify data residency commitments for Dedicated vs Private.
- Subprocessor list and notification cadence (your legal asked for 30 days notice).
- Whether the Private/on-prem package includes our optional audit-logging agent and how logs are shared.

High-level suggestion from my side: add a deployment-mode exhibit that ties the relevant clauses to Dedicated vs Private (e.g., data-at-rest encryption scope, key custody options). That keeps the core DPA small and makes mode-specific obligations explicit.

I also flagged a DocuSign route for execution when terms are final. Happy to coordinate next steps.

Best,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Emily Jones <emily.jones@acmehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>, legal@infracorp.com
Date: 2026-10-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: Deployment-mode data governance and e-sign flow (Dedicated vs Private)

Jonas,

Thanks — received the redlines. A few clarifications from our side before we proceed:
1) For Dedicated we need a statement that customer data will not leave the selected region unless explicitly requested. Is that something Redwood can commit to in the DPA exhibit?
2) For Private/on-prem we need guidance on what evidence you will provide for the audit-logging agent — a configuration checklist and a sample log export would suffice.
3) On subprocessors: Acme requires a 45-day notification window for new subprocessors that will process PHI.

I copied InfraCorp Legal since they handle our third-party reviews — they will push back if the notice window is shorter.

Emily Jones
Director, IT Sourcing — Acme Health
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T08:24:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: DPA: Deployment-mode data governance and e-sign flow (Dedicated vs Private)

Forwarding Emily's notes. Quick thoughts:
- Region residency for Dedicated: operationally we can pin instances to region and document it, but need to confirm routing/fallback policy in the event of capacity constraints. Suggest we add a fallback paragraph to the exhibit that permits cross-region failover for short windows and requires notice.
- 45-day subprocessors for PHI feels long compared to our standard 30 days; need commercialization/legal sign-off.
- For Private: we can produce the config checklist and a sanitized sample log. That should meet their evidence ask.

I'll draft proposed language for the deployment-mode exhibit and loop in Priya for legal redline.

-Neha
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Emily Jones <emily.jones@acmehealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: Deployment-mode data governance and e-sign flow (Dedicated vs Private)

Emily —

Appreciate the precision. Draft language attached in the PDF highlights:
- Dedicated: clause that binds Redwood to regional residency for customer data and requires 72-hour notice for planned cross-region migrations; emergency failover allowed with post-event disclosure within 24 hours.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): exhibit that lists optional components (audit-logging agent, KMS integration instructions) and describes evidence deliverables (config checklist and sample logs).
- Subprocessors: proposed compromise is 30-day notice plus a contractual right for Acme to object to new subprocessors processing PHI; if objection is reasonable, parties will negotiate in good faith.

If that sounds acceptable I can prepare a redline we can share with Acme and InfraCorp Legal.

Regards,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: InfraCorp Legal <legal@infracorp.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Emily Jones <emily.jones@acmehealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: Deployment-mode data governance and e-sign flow (Dedicated vs Private)

Thanks for the draft, Priya. A couple practical points from Acme's counsel:
- 72-hour notice for planned migrations is workable; emergency failover must include strict scope limits (e.g., max 48 hours unless Acme approves extension).
- The objection right to subprocessors is good, but Acme wants a defined escalation path and a timeline (15 days to raise objection, 30 days to remediate or escalate to arbitration).
- For PHI, InfraCorp requests that any subprocessors be SOC 2 Type II and that Redwood supply the last SOC report on request (redacted copy acceptable).

We'll review the redline once you post it.

— InfraCorp Legal (Andrea Silva)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Emily Jones <emily.jones@acmehealth.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: Deployment-mode data governance and e-sign flow (Dedicated vs Private)

Team —

Thanks everyone for the quick turn. Next steps:
1) Priya — can you post the redlined DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3_redlines.pdf) with the deployment-mode exhibit added by EOD PDT tomorrow?
2) Neha — confirm operational statement re: region pinning and the brief failover window language so we can accept InfraCorp's 48-hour emergency cap.
3) Sergio — please prepare the SOC 2 summary and the sanitized log sample to attach.
4) Emily/InfraCorp — once you confirm the subprocessors timeline (15/30) we will route the final redline via DocuSign (link above) for signatures.

If we can all align this week, legal has agreed to a one-click e-sign route. Happy to jump on a short call if needed.

Best,
Jonas
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3_redlines.pdf (redline), Acme_DataFlow_Spec.xlsx (dataflow mapping)
